diagnostic_approaches.name: Ren et al. 2020 CNN-based vocal cord lesion classifier

diagnostic_approaches.name: Kuo et al. 2021 AI-assisted diagnostic system for laryngeal lesions

diagnostic_approaches.name: Zhao et al. 2022 DCNN-based vocal cord lesion diagnostic system

diagnostic_approaches.name: Chen et al. 2023 3D VOSNet for vocal cord/glottis segmentation

diagnostic_approaches.name: DL models for pharyngeal cancer using WLI/NBI/BLI (Atsuko 2020; Mitsuhiro 2021)

since not only is such a bronchoscope very expensive but also it is hard for a bronchoscopist to operate.

leading to a less reliable bronchoscopic AI system.

diagnostic_approaches.name: YOLOX (You Only Look Once) for lesion detection
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Lesion detection (bronchoscopic/endoscopic images)
criteria_or_scoring: Category prediction loss (BCE with logits loss)
Bounding box regression loss (Io U difference)

limitations: Single-stage methods may be slightly less accurate than two-stage methods.

problems_observed.finding: Lack of standardization in bronchoscopy examinations
problems_observed.details: Accuracy is greatly affected by the operator’s experience, habits, and skills, leading to unstable and even mistaken results—described as a lack of standardization. No specific adherence metrics or rates are provided.
problems_observed.reference: Chapter abstract/introduction (Cao et al., Artificial Intelligence in Respiratory Endoscopy, 2025)

problems_observed.finding: Interobserver variability leading to inconsistent diagnosis and treatment
problems_observed.details: Different endoscopists and physicians may interpret the same lesion differently, causing inconsistent diagnostic results and corresponding treatment. No explicit guideline comparison or statistics are given.

problems_observed.finding: Blind spots during bronchoscopic examination suggest incomplete systematic inspection
problems_observed.details: The chapter highlights the need for real-time monitoring and automatic prompts for missed areas, implying current practice may leave blind spots unexamined. No quantitative data on miss rates are provided.
problems_observed.reference: Introduction and section topic on blind spot monitoring

problems_observed.details: Similar quality control issues to bronchoscopy are noted for NPL, with a dedicated section on 'Quality Control Issues with NPL'. No specific adherence metrics or detailed examples are provided.

guideline_adherence.implication: Operator-dependent variability and lack of standardized workflows can lead to missed lesions, misdiagnoses, and inconsistent treatment. While the chapter does not provide explicit guideline adherence data, it implies gaps relative to standardized examination protocols; AI-assisted systems aim to improve quality control, reduce blind spots, and standardize practice, potentially improving patient outcomes.

technology_and_technique.topic: AI-assisted bronchoscopy quality control (blind spot monitoring)
technology_and_technique.summary: Real-time monitoring during bronchoscopy with automatic prompts for missed areas to standardize the examination and reduce operator dependence. Described benefits include improved diagnostic precision, high automation, low cost, stability, and mitigation of human fatigue. No specific diagnostic yield percentages or safety event rates reported.
technology_and_technique.reference: Cao Z, Ye B, Zhou Y, Liu B. Artificial Intelligence in Respiratory Endoscopy. In: Yarmus L et al., Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer Nature Switzerland; 2025. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_2-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Automatic diagnosis of bronchial lesions (CADe/CADx) in bronchoscopy
technology_and_technique.summary: AI systems preprocess bronchoscopic images and analyze lesion morphology, color, and texture to aid detection and diagnosis. The chapter states improved diagnostic accuracy and consistency through training on large clinical datasets but provides no quantitative accuracy, sensitivity/specificity, or yield percentages.

AI-based enhancement aims to improve visualization quality of bronchoscopic images to support lesion recognition and diagnostic performance. No comparative metrics (e.g., signal-to-noise, reader performance, or diagnostic yield changes) are reported.

technology_and_technique.topic: Deep learning for branch recognition (quality control in bronchoscopy)
technology_and_technique.summary: Deep learning models are used to recognize bronchial branches as part of quality control to standardize bronchoscopy navigation and reduce missed areas. No specific accuracy rates, coverage percentages, or time-efficiency gains are provided.

technology_and_technique.topic: Deep learning for lesion detection in bronchoscopy
technology_and_technique.summary: Lesion detection methods using deep neural networks are described to automate identification of bronchial abnormalities. The chapter does not provide sensitivity/specificity, AUC, or per-lesion diagnostic yield statistics.

technology_and_technique.topic: AI in nasopharyngolaryngoscopy (NPL): quality control and lesion identification
technology_and_technique.summary: AI applications include quality control for NPL, categorization of vocal cord abnormalities, and identification of laryngeal/pharyngeal and nasal/nasopharyngeal lesions. The text emphasizes standardization and diagnostic support but does not report quantitative yields or safety outcomes.

technology_and_technique.topic: Expert-robot multidisciplinary team (MDT) for pulmonary nodule assessment
technology_and_technique.summary: Combines human experts with AI to assess 3D longest diameter, volume, and density of lung nodules and to create personalized diagnostic plans. Intended to leverage AI precision while mitigating false positives/negatives via human oversight. No prospective trial results or diagnostic yield/safety statistics are provided.

Respiratory AI has been more established in chest X-ray, CT, lung function, and ventilation; AI in bronchoscopy and NPL is emerging. The chapter contrasts maturity with GI endoscopy (where CADe/CADx are widely integrated) but provides no direct comparative effectiveness or head-to-head performance data between modalities (e.g., bronchoscopy vs other diagnostic techniques).

technology_and_technique.topic: Tips to improve procedural performance with AI
technology_and_technique.summary: Suggested operational advantages include real-time blind-spot prompts, standardized workflows, integration of multimodal imaging, and reduction of user variability and fatigue. The chapter does not quantify improvements (e.g., reduced miss rates, procedure time, or complication rates).

technology_and_technique.topic: Patient selection considerations for AI-assisted endoscopy
technology_and_technique.summary: AI support is discussed for patients undergoing bronchoscopy and NPL and for those with pulmonary nodules (via expert-robot MDT). No explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, risk stratification thresholds, or safety stratification data are provided.

points: 15 Abstract Bronchoscopy plays an important role in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases which can directly observe the internal conditions of the trachea and bronchi

However, the accuracy of its examination results is greatly affected by the experience, habits, and skill levels of endoscopists, resulting in unstable and even mistaken examination results, i.e., there is a lack of standardization in bronchoscopy

summary: Monitor 31 bronchial sites for coverage and examination time; prompt revisits for missed or obscured areas.
Flag short examinations (e.g., <2 min) as at-risk for missed spots; encourage adequate dwell time.
Assess image quality (illuminance, contrast, noise, blur); discard low-quality frames or enhance before analysis.
Use a trained classifier (e.g., VGG/Goog Le Net/Res Net) for branch recognition to support standardized documentation.
Run a single-stage detector (e.g., YOLOX) to localize airway lesions and label benign vs malignant patterns; auto-measure size and depth as supported.
Export annotated images, lesion metadata, and coverage logs for reporting and QA.
